# [TASK] Add negative-path test coverage across the ai-service surface

## Task

The ai-service suite has effectively no negative-path coverage, which is why the error-mapping and input-bounds defects in the sibling tasks are invisible to CI.

Before this review, the integration tests and the contract test asserted only 2xx paths plus a single 404 ownership case, and `AiGrpcServiceTest` covered only UUID parsing. Nothing posted an invalid body, a negative or oversized `k`, an oversized `count`, malformed JSON, or an over-limit multipart upload — so an implementation returning 500 for all of them passed green, and a fix could be reverted without a single test failing.

The security-hardening pass in this same review added negative-path tests for the endpoints it touched. This task is to extend that to the rest of the surface, so the fixes in the sibling tasks land with tests that would actually catch a regression.

Separately, `AiGrpcServiceTest.setUp()` has no Javadoc, which `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s documentation standard explicitly extends to helper and setup methods.

## Parent Story

Parent: #186

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every ai-service endpoint has at least one test asserting its behaviour on invalid input, not only on the happy path
- [x] The gRPC transport has negative-path coverage beyond UUID parsing — at minimum a blank message and an out-of-range count
- [x] Each test fails if the corresponding validation or mapping is removed (verified by actually removing it once, not assumed)
- [x] `AiGrpcServiceTest.setUp()` has a Javadoc, per the repo's documentation standard

**Hours:** 4
